hypotheses: Field: Prop. 12.4 holds for any fields k ⊆ K, so K-general coefficients fit (take k = target K, K = C). Dimension: it allows any d × l matrix; the x_i are only k-linearly independent. The extension F, V_0 and the w_j do not appear in it; they enter only in my derivation. Basis order: a finite basis of the V_0-part of the entries first, then the w's last. Independence holds because the w's are algebraically independent over F ⊇ V_0, K. Genericity: Prop. 12.4 has no transcendence hypothesis at all, and the whole of the target's hypothesis on the w's is used in the supplied argument. Conjugation: absent. It is needed only for Theorem A, where F = Q̄(u) contains ū = ρ/u. Rank one and configurations: not mentioned there. Theorem A also needs Lemma 12.16 / Exercise 12.10 (p. 443: rows and columns independent, dim E ≤ 3 gives rank ≥ (d+l)/4). That is the printed m = 0 case, and the target already names it as nearby.

explanation:
Prop. 12.4 is present, but it is only a block normal form. Separation is not printed; I had to derive it.

Derivation. M = (x_i y_j) has every 2×2 minor zero, also after k-equivalence (x' ⊗ y'). Apply 12.4 with the w's as top variables. Take the least t with r_t > 0 at a w-level, and W its variable. Then all entries lie in the span without higher w's; only diagonal entries of M_tt involve W, with nonzero coefficient.

If r_t ≥ 2, a diagonal 2×2 minor has W²-coefficient nonzero, and W is transcendental over F(other w's): contradiction. So r_t = 1, with entry cW+a; other entries b_j, c_i, D_ij omit W.

The minor (cW+a)D_ij = b_j c_i gives D = 0, then b_j c_i = 0 for all i, j. So b = 0 or c = 0, which makes a column or row zero (p,q ≥ 2), contradicting independence. Hence no w-level occurs and all entries lie in V_0.

The real content is this transcendence step, which is short and in the style of the p. 422 proof. The citation supports the "routine" label and "extends the argument", but it is not a printed find.
